before: A sealed interface specifies permitted direct subtypes. Outcome permits only Success and Failure here. Those final classes cannot be subclassed further.

A permitted ordinary class must choose final, sealed, or non-sealed as required by the sealed hierarchy rules. non-sealed deliberately reopens that branch; sealed does not mean the objects are immutable.
An unrelated class cannot simply implement Outcome unless it is permitted. These top-level declarations share the same source file and unnamed package, satisfying the location rule for this example.

Expected output or behavior: true
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain the difference between final and non-sealed for a permitted branch before experimenting locally. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A sealed interface limits its direct implementations: the types that implement it without an intermediate parent. Outcome lists Success and Failure in its permits clause, so only those direct types are allowed here.

An ordinary class allowed by a sealed type chooses how its own branch continues. final allows no child classes. sealed limits its children. non-sealed allows the branch to grow normally. These words do not freeze object data.
A new direct implementation must be allowed by the sealed declaration. Location rules also apply. These types share one file and the unnamed package, so they meet the location rule here.
The program prints true because outcome points to a Success object rather than null. Success is allowed by the permits list.
The quiz adds another direct implementation without adding its name to permits. Check the allowed names before considering its body.

choices: Other is automatically added to the permitted list

after.question: Add final class Other implements Outcome {} without changing permits. What happens?
choices: Java automatically adds Other to permits.
Compilation fails because Other is not permitted.
after.explanation: The explicit permits list allows Success and Failure. Other is not on that list.
